title: Payment-History Down Payment Share for Seller Settlements
content:
**Rule.** On a spread failed-sale charge of a Real Estate Service Contracts listing order, the down payment taken from the seller reflects the seller's payment history with Bridgewell. The payment-history share follows the returned payments recorded on the seller's Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts and Utility Line Protection Plans in the twelve months before the settlement date, the returned payments on both products being counted together:

| Returned payments in the twelve months before the settlement date | Payment-history share |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 30% |
| exactly 1 | 15% |
| none | no payment-history share |

The payment-history share is added once to the down payment share. The down payment is the open failed-sale balance times the down payment share, which is never below zero, rounded to the cent, and it is taken with the first settlement payment.

## Records read

The billing entries of the seller's Homeowner Service Contracts contracts and Utility Line Protection Plans plans that are recorded as returned payments, with their entry dates.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical sellers)

- One returned payment on the seller's homeowner contract and one on the seller's line plan, both within the twelve months: 2 returned payments, share 30%.
- One returned payment fourteen months before the settlement date and none since: no returned payment in the window, no payment-history share.
- On an open failed-sale balance of $800.00, a share of 30% gives a down payment contribution of $240.00.
